---
title: "Data downloads and caching"
---

The IBL atlas downloads its data the first time it is used and keeps it on disk. Later uses
read the saved copy, so each dataset downloads once.

## What downloads, and how large it is

The atlas itself downloads once per resolution. The additional datasets download only when they
are first loaded.

| Data | Approximate size |
|---|---|
| Atlas at 25 µm | 40 MB |
| Gene expression (AGEA) | 2.6 GB |
| MERFISH | 630 MB |
| Depths | 350 MB |
| Lipids | 105 MB |
| Flat maps | 30 MB |

## Where the data comes from

The data comes from two public sources, and neither needs an account or credentials:

- **The Allen Institute**, for the atlas volumes: the Allen Mouse Brain Atlas (2015) with the
  2017 region annotations.
- **The IBL public data store** (the `ibl-brain-wide-map-public` S3 bucket), for the flat maps,
  the depths, the genomics and lipid volumes, and the connectivity tables described in
  [External data in the common space](external-data-in-the-common-space.qmd).

## Where the data is saved

The data is saved in the cache directory of ONE, the IBL data-access package, which installs
with the IBL atlas. By default, the atlas files are in:

```
~/Downloads/ONE/openalyx.internationalbrainlab.org/histology/ATLAS/Needles/Allen
```

To save them somewhere else, see
[Save the atlas data somewhere else](../how-to/install.qmd#save-the-atlas-data-somewhere-else).
